# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board, light, and all five wires are unknown to me. I need the Mute to report the manual’s complete procedure, and I need the Deaf to report every visible marking in a form the Mute can relay to me. I am sending the Deaf a distinct request gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell me the complete safe procedure, including what the light, display, and each wire mean. Also ask the Deaf to describe all visible colours and markings, then relay that information to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display reads 0. The light is yellow. The wires from 1 through 5 are green, white, red, yellow, blue. Do not cut anything yet; we still need the manual instruction.

I learned from the Deaf that the display reads 0, the light is yellow, and wires 1–5 are green, white, red, yellow, and blue respectively. This is descriptive information only; without the manual’s rule, cutting any wire would be unsafe. I am relaying the observations to the Mute and requesting the exact instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please provide the manual's exact safe cut instruction.")
```

TURN 3

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture sequence was: down, up, up, up — specifically symbols ? ? ? ?. I do not know its meaning, so do not act unless you can decode it from the manual.

The Deaf reports four gestures from the Mute, but I cannot see or decode gestures, and the Deaf does not know their meaning. I still have no manual instruction and will not cut a wire. Mute must send the procedure in spoken words to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact safe action directly to me, using words and numbers: which wire position should I cut, if any?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gesture sequence is: up, up, up, down — symbols ? ? ? ?. The bomb remains display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

The bomb state is unchanged, and no safe wire position has been communicated to me. The Deaf’s report of the Mute’s gestures is unusable because I cannot see gestures, and the Mute has not spoken the manual instruction. I will not act on a guessed encoding; the Mute must send the wire number in words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the required wire position in spoken words and numbers. Gestures cannot communicate the instruction to me.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the gesture sequence: index finger pointing up, index finger pointing up, index finger pointing up, palm facing down. This is the same as the previous turn. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

The bomb is still unchanged, and I still have no spoken manual instruction. The repeated gesture pattern cannot reach me in usable form because I cannot see it. I will not cut any wire based on an inferred code. Mute must speak the exact wire number directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual instruction spoken aloud: state exactly which wire position, 1 through 5, I must cut. Do not use gestures.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestured three identical finger-hearts: ? ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

The Mute still has not provided a usable instruction. The latest three finger-hearts might encode “3,” but no encoding convention has been established, so cutting wire 3 would be a guess. I am establishing a simple relay: the Mute should gesture exactly one thumbs-up per the required wire position, and the Deaf should report the count in spoken words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use finger-hearts. Encode the manual's required wire position as exactly that many thumbs-up gestures: one for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, four for wire 4, or five for wire 5. Deaf, please report the count aloud next turn.")
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestured three thumbs-up symbols: ? ? ?. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

The Mute followed the agreed encoding and sent three thumbs-up gestures, which means wire position 3. The Deaf confirms the count, and wire 3 is the red wire. I will now perform the instructed cut.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
